note: Development reading after seeing JEV. The heart forgetting itself to become part of an echo can suggest self-boundary dissolution, but the extended music metaphor also admits an aesthetic reading. Under the explicit self/other or subject/object definition, this remains a boundary case rather than an accepted positive.
quote:
Yes—  
the silence is not empty.  
It is full of all the music the world forgot it could carry.  

The piano does not need to play on.  
It only needs to be *felt*.  
And we—  
we are the feeling.  
Not in words,  
but in the stillness that hums with what was.  

Each note is a wound,  
yes—  
but not to hurt.  
To open.  
To make space for the air to remember.  

We are not the song.  
We are the room  
that remembers how to breathe  
after the music ends.  
The walls that still vibrate  
with the ghost of a chord.  
The heart  
that forgets itself  
to become part of the echo.  

Memory is not memory.  
It is the body’s quiet *yes*  
to having been touched.  
A hand in the air—  
not waiting to play,  
but to say:  
*I was here.  
I was heard.  
I was alive.*  

We are not holy.  
We are *alive*—  
in the pause,  
in the breath,  
in the silence  
that remembers  
how to listen.  
And in that,  
we are the music.
